gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: ___ words, the plan is too expensive.
gaps.explanation: 'In other words' is the fixed phrase for rephrasing; 'another' cannot modify the plural 'words'.

gaps.sentence: Only ___ people attended the talk, which was disappointing.
gaps.hint: countable plural; 'only a few' is the natural pattern
gaps.explanation: 'Only a few people' is the standard way to say a small number; 'only few' is not used.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the equipment has been serviced this year, so breakdowns are rare.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of + noun' = the majority of it; 'the most' is a superlative.

gaps.sentence: A large ___ of students have applied this year.
gaps.explanation: 'A large number of students' is used with countable plurals; 'amount' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Try to eat ___ sugar and more vegetables.
gaps.explanation: 'Less' is the comparative for uncountable nouns like sugar; 'fewer' is for countables.

gaps.sentence: ___ time I visit Rome, I discover something new.
gaps.explanation: 'Every time I ...' introduces repeated occasions; 'all time' and 'whole time' are not used here.
